answer: Each of 532 aliases needs its own aged keys, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. A pGP key age with keyserver publication date works as the gate: a public key published on keyservers years ago. The wharf check is what stops the copy-paste farm: The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. The raven record is public, the falcon cost is per identity, and 532 aliases cost 532 times one honest seat.
